text:
alyssa: heads up — after the NCCL 2.27.1 bump in us-west, we started seeing intermittent hangs on multi-GPU inference jobs that touch mixed-card hosts (A100 + A10).
raj: saw this too, reproduces with our small repro script when p2p enabled. hangs inside ncclCommInitRank.
marco: can you paste the stack / logs?
alyssa: paste from one failing pod: ```
I0314 02:12:07.123456 1 nccl.cc:210] ncclCommInitRank() tid=4272 
[0] NCCL INFO Call to ncclCommInitRank blocked for > 120s
#0 0x7f6a3a7a in ncclCommInitRank()
#1 0x7f6a3b21 in some_internal_init()
#2 0x55f4bd in main
```
hannah: same stack here. timeline: we rolled NCCL across canary pool at 02:00, then staged to us-west at 02:05. failures started ~02:11.
zach: are these nodes running mixed drivers/OS/kernel? which cuda?
raj: hosts are CUDA 12.3 driver 535.xx on A100 hosts, and 11.8 driver 520.xx on A10 hosts (we've got mixed kernel modules because some boxes haven't been rebooted since driver swap). suspect ABI mismatch.
marco: interesting — NCCL 2.27 claims better multi-arch fallback but also changed p2p / nvlink discovery logic. mixed driver/kernel combos have historically been brittle.
alyssa: customer impact: a handful of Dedicated jobs hit 30s RPC timeouts and timed out on tokenized inference, SLO alarm noise. no full fleet outage but backpressure on queued requests.
hannah: current mitigations: we throttled canary to 5% and paused the us-west rollout. also turned off p2p (env var NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1) on a subset to confirm.
raj: disabling p2p reduced hang frequency in the test repro (from 4/5 runs to 1/10) so it's a good short-term mitigation.
zach: downside: disabling p2p increases latency and GPU-to-GPU transfer cost; some latency-sensitive customers will degrade. need comms.
marco: ops plan proposal: 1) pause rollout globally; 2) pin us-west back to NCCL 2.26 for nodes that had upgrades; 3) run a controlled canary where we reboot nodes to align driver/kernel first; 4) vendor engagement with NVIDIA for a root-cause trace.
alyssa: can we avoid full rollback? rollback will require draining ~120 nodes and will reduce capacity by ~15% during the window.
hannah: we could do targeted rollback only on mixed-arch racks (we have labels). that would affect ~40 nodes (~5% capacity). cheaper.
raj: to validate, we need kernel module versions and nvlink topology per host. I can run a quick inventory with this: ```
for n in $(cat /srv/pool/mixed-racks); do ssh $n 'nvidia-smi -q | grep -E "Driver Version|CUDA Version"; modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic; lspci | grep -i nvlink'; done
```
marco: also collect a strace from a hung process and /proc/interrupts, and include NCCL_TRACE=INFO log.
zach: oncall-bot scheduled a rolling drain + patch window for tonight 00:30–02:30 PT if we decide rollback.
oncall-bot: scheduled maintenance window: rollback-nccl-2.27 -> 2.26 (us-west mixed racks), start=2105591400, end=2105598600, owners=eng-runtime, message=will drain nodes, expect 15% capacity impact. :warning:
alyssa: i'd prefer the targeted rollback plan; let's confirm which racks are truly mixed. raj, can you produce a list within 30m?
raj: on it, will attach inventory here shortly.
hannah: I'll draft a short customer note in #customer-success if we have to pause Dedicated capacity, mention limited impact and that we're reverting a library update.
marco: follow-up: we should add a preflight check to our rollout pipeline: fail if driver/kernel mismatch across peers or if nvlink topology differs from baseline.
alyssa: agreed — add a gating check: "peer-driver-consensus" that queries all nodes in the target slot and fails the canary if >5% divergence.
zach: ops-schedule question — if we rollback, do we need a temporary increase in burst-capacity elsewhere? we might auto-scale Dedicated pools in other regions to cover slots. cost estimate?
hannah: 40-node deficit for 2 hours at reserved rates -> ballpark $1.2k. we can absorb but flag finance.
raj: inventory attached: nodes labelled rack-A1..A6 show mixed driver versions on GPUs: A1-3 have driver 535, A4-6 have 520. A4 and A5 have older kernel 5.10, others 5.15.
marco: ok that's our smoking gun (kernel mismatch + mixed drivers). engage NVIDIA with kernel module traces. also try repro with the exact kernel combo in our lab.
alyssa: action items: raj -> full node list + nvlink topology (30m), hannah -> comms draft (15m), marco -> repro on lab cluster (2h), zach -> confirm rollback window and autoscale plan (1h).
raj: posted inventory CSV to GCS: gs://redwood-infra/nccl-investigations/2105556667-inventory.csv
marco: also note: some long-tail hung traces show syscalls blocked in ioctl to /dev/nvidiactl — might be kernel module deadlock.
alyssa: thanks team. keep updates in this thread and ping @oncall if we hit an uplift. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: incident alert auto-created: INC-8234, priority=P2, linked-thread=2105556667
zach: will update the rollout doc to include the peer-driver-consensus gate after rollback is complete.
hannah: comms draft posted in #customer-success-drafts, please review.
raj: inventory complete, starting targeted rollback on racks A4..A6 in 40m unless objections.
marco: no objections from me.
alyssa: ack. proceeding to targeted rollback plan. keep calm, and we’ll triage vendor escalation in parallel.
